title: Hosted API - cache TTL vs PPK & margin sandbox
summary: Sandbox worksheet exploring how varying prefix/KV cache TTL and hit-rate profiles change per-token COGS (PPK) and gross margin across model families and regions. Includes worked examples, sensitivity slices, and short ops/experiment runbook.
content:
Problem statement:
We want a lightweight, understandable mapping from cache configuration (TTL, scope) and observed hit rates to incremental PPK reduction and margin impact for hosted API customers. This is a companion to regional-sku work but focused on cache tuning and short-term ops wins.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Workload: mix = 55% chat (sessioned), 30% single-turn prompts, 15% embeddings (charged separately but included here for infra egress).
- Representative model families: small (rwd-3B-q), medium (rwd-7B-q), large (rwd-70B-fp16).
- GPU amortized cost per token (compute-only): 0.0009 USD/token (large), 0.00028 USD/token (medium), 0.00012 USD/token (small) at baseline batching/slotting.
- Network egress & infra misc per token: 0.00003 USD/token (global average).
- Cacheable token fraction: prefix tokens only. Average prefix length (chat context) = 120 tokens, average generation length = 80 tokens; so cacheable share of request = ~60%.
- Cache serving cost per cache hit: 0.000002 USD/token equivalent (hot path memcache + serialization).
- Cache miss penalty: full compute cost for prefix tokens (no KV reuse), but we still amortize autoregressive generation for suffix as usual.

Key levers/scenarios: TTL options: 0s (no cache), 30s, 5m, 1h, 24h. Hit profile mapping (example 1 - high locality app): 0s=0%, 30s=25%, 5m=45%, 1h=60%, 24h=65%. Example 2 (low locality): 0s=0%, 30s=8%, 5m=12%, 1h=15%, 24h=17%.

Worked example (medium model rwd-7B-q, regional bucket: us-west):
- Baseline compute ppk (no cache) = 0.00028 + network 0.00003 = 0.00031 USD/token.
- Prefix tokens per request = 120 * 0.6 = 72 tokens saved on hit.
- If hit rate = 45% (5m TTL): expected per-request token savings = 72 * 0.45 = 32.4 tokens saved (compute avoided).
- Compute avoided per-request in USD = 32.4 * 0.00028 = 0.009072 USD. Normalize to per-token (divide by average tokens billed per request -- here 200 tokens) => per-token reduction = 0.009072 / 200 = 0.00004536 USD/token saved.
- Net cost of serving hits (cache cost) = 32.4 * 0.000002 = 0.0000648 USD per request => per-token = 0.000000324 USD/token (negligible).
- New PPK approx = 0.00031 - 0.00004536 + 0.000000324 = 0.000264964 USD/token. ~14.5% reduction.

Sensitivity slices (by model family):
- Small model (rwd-3B-q): smaller base compute ppk => absolute savings smaller, % savings lower (ex: 6-8% at 45% hit).
- Large model (rwd-70B-fp16): base ppk much higher => absolute savings large (e.g., 0.0009 * 32.4 / 200 = 0.0001458 USD/token -> ~16% relative).

Regional adjustments:
- ap-south and eu-north have higher network/infra overhead (+8–12% COGS), reduce % margin uplift slightly.
- regions with higher GPU amortization (spot vs reserved mix) show different marginal impact; attach simple scalar table below.

Quick scalar table (example numbers):
- Region scalar: us-east=1.00, us-west=1.02, eu-west=1.08, ap-south=1.12
- Model base compute ppk (baseline region scalar applied): small=0.00012*scalar, medium=0.00028*scalar, large=0.0009*scalar.

Policy recommendations (ops + product):
1) Default TTL: 5m for sessioned chat by default; rationale: large marginal win vs small memory footprint and low risk of staleness for most chat workloads.
2) Tiered TTL per customer segment: PLG/free: 30s, Scale customers (committed): 1h by default, Enterprise security-sensitive: opt-out ability for privacy/PII concerns.
3) Experimental: aggressive 24h TTL for known high-locality systems (embedding-backed re-ranking apps where prompts are repeated).
4) Expose a billing transparency doc snippet showing expected % margin improvement by model family and TTL to reduce CS ticket volume.

Experiment runbook (short):
- Metric to measure: realized cache hit rate (per-customer), change in observed p95 latency, delta in per-token COGS as measured by infra accounting.
- A/B cohort: 5% traffic with TTL 5m vs control at 30s for 3 weeks.
- Safety checks: monitor hallucination/regression signals (quality eval set) for potential stale-context regressions.
- Success criteria: >8% PPK reduction for top 10% of customers by volume without >2% latency regression.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need accurate distribution of prefix lengths by customer segment (we currently use 120 tokens global avg).
- How to tie cache invalidation semantics to tool/function-calling workflows (structured output can change staleness requirements).
- Investigate multi-region cache coherence cost vs local region-only caches.

Appendix: quick calculation checklist for SRE / finance sync:
- Pull per-region GPU amort (hourly) and convert to ppk using tok/sec baseline derived from typical batch.
- Extract observed average prompt lengths and session reuse percent from logs (last 90d).
- Compute hit-rate envelope for TTL options using 7-day sliding window.

Notes to self: connect with Ellie on prefetched-KV proposals and with Ravi on including dedicated-reserve blends into regional scalar. Share this sheet in Tuesday optimize sync for prioritization.

Example CSV export (preview) - columns: region,model_family,ttl,hit_rate,base_ppk,new_ppk,ppk_delta_pct,notes

us-west,medium,5m,0.45,0.00031,0.000265,14.5%,sample-run
us-west,large,5m,0.45,0.00093,0.00078,16.2%,sample-run
e-west,medium,5m,0.12,0.000335,0.000318,5.1%,low-locality

End of sheet - sanity check: small absolute numbers but cumulative monthly savings can be material at scale (millions of tokens per day). Next: convert this into a lightweight simulator notebook and include as part of the token-econ workbench.
